columns.name: password
columns._evidence: Synthetic modelling column: LedgerSMB stores account credentials in Postgres roles (pg_authid), not on users. The User table has no password column (only notify_password, a password-expiry interval). This column models 'can this username+password sign in' so the login-gated surface is reachable, consistent with the OAuth-only repo pattern.

username.description: The account username to sign in with.

_evidence.entity_why: primary effect row_insert lands on this table
_evidence.ref_code: sub authenticate { my ($request)=@_; if ($request->{_req}->content_length > 4096){ return unauthorized(); } ... my $r=$json->decode($body); if(!$r->{login}||!$r->{password}){return unauthorized();} $r->{company}||=$settings->{default_db}; my $target=$request->{_create_session}->($r->{login},$r->{password},$r->{company}); return $target if $target; $request->{_req}->env->{'lsmb.session'}->{company_path}=md5_hex($r->{company}); my $token=$request->{_req}->env->{'lsmb.session'}->{company_path}; return [HTTP_OK, ..., qq|{"target":"$token/erp.pl?user=$user"}|]; }
_evidence.note: auth account_entity=User. Real LedgerSMB credentials live in Postgres roles (pg_authid) via login.pm; the User table has no password column. A synthetic `password` column has been added to model 'this username+password signs in', consistent with the OAuth-only repo pattern. _auth_gravity_mismatch (46 FKs to Entity) is resolved: Entity is the business contact, not the login; User.username is the login identity.
